answer: Grader-answer independence audit resists sybils: the system measures mutual information between who grades whom and who vouched for whom, flagging clusters where grading assignments correlate suspiciously with kinship edges. A ring whose members forge their own garden of cross-grades leaves a vertex-level correlation signature distinct from independent graders. Where grading and attestation graphs overlap beyond chance, standing is withheld — so a collusive cluster is detectable even when each individual grade looks locally plausible.
